findings: Windows processes run in the disposable VM; accepted draw and clear requests run on the physical Panther Lake NPU. The indirect display is the sole active guest display during ten received frames. A Mac SDL viewer presents the received images.

588 successful NPU requests comprise 17 prewarm draws, 477 live draws and 94 live clears. All 588 have successful acknowledgements. One additional DWM request is rejected by the point-texture specialization.

The desktop and Start menu become visible. Start first appears 190.090593 seconds after the Windows-key action. Escape is sent later, but the last sole-display frame still shows Start. No responsive interactive desktop has been established.

The first Start-visible frame arrives after the DWM rejection. Sole-display topology and accepted NPU receipts do not prove that Windows performed no internal recovery or fallback after the rejected draw.

The rejected capture has a 642x661 target, but its geometry covers only the top 440 rows, sampling a 642x440 region from origin (191,328) of a 1024x768 source. The crop specialization requires full-target coverage. Its capture replay also fails during executor construction because the old crop-only oracle assumes all 661 rows are sampled.

A diagnostic replay routes the same capture to the existing general triangle renderer. Both CPU and NPU pass the independent full-image scalar oracle with exact coverage of 282480 samples and zero pixel error. The two resulting 1697448-byte images are byte-identical. This establishes a routing defect, not an inability of the NPU to render this draw.

The observer stops for a recorded DWM rejection. Both custom drivers and stream configuration are removed. The input controller later saves a stale frame after sole-display topology has ended; that snapshot is not evidence of an Escape response.
The general-renderer diagnostic is separate from the installed trial. Physical Delta scanout, broad application coverage, a usable full desktop and improved Tahoma performance remain unverified.
